Subject: MSA clause reconciliation + implementation fee — initial redlines

Hannah,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are Atlas's redlines to the Order Form and a short PDF with line-item comments on MSA Section 5 (Implementation & Acceptance). Two quick items we need clarity on before we can proceed to our SOW sign-off:

- Is the implementation fee refundable in the event of a delayed go-live beyond 90 days? Our Ops team wants either a pro rata refund or a credit mechanism.
- The Order Form shows dedicated capacity ramping in month 2. We asked for an earlier ramp (month 1); your legal has kept the ramp language ambiguous. Could you confirm intent so we can budget headcount?

I've also flagged a data residency sentence in Section 7 that we assumed was an Atlas-only obligation — please confirm.

Attachments: Atlas_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx, MSA_section_5_comments.pdf

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Sr. Contracts Manager | Atlas Health

Subject: Re: MSA clause reconciliation + implementation fee — initial redlines

Maya —

Appreciate the detailed notes and the redline package. Quick responses up-front:
- Implementation fee: Redwood's standard is non-refundable unless a termination for cause by the customer occurs. That said, we can offer a pro rata credit tied to milestone completion windows (we've used this with other healthcare customers).
- Ramp timing: our commercial intent was month 1 availability for burst capacity but steady-state reserved capacity in month 2. If Atlas needs a committed month-1 reserved pool, that will change the fee schedule.
- Data residency: Redwood's default is logical isolation with hosting region controls, not physical segregation unless specified in a Private deployment addendum.

Looping in Karthik and Laura from Legal/RevOps to triage suggested contract language and price sensitivity. Karthik — can you take point on proposed language for Section 5 (implementation refund/credit), and Laura, please review the ramp wording so procurement gets a clear statement.

I'll propose a short redline call tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-14T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA clause reconciliation + implementation fee — draft language

Team / Maya —

I reviewed the attachments and drafted two short options for Section 5 that should address Atlas's ask without opening broad refund exposure. Summary below; full tracked-changes are in my attachment (MSA_section_5_comments.pdf).

Option A (preferred): milestone-based credit — if go-live is delayed beyond 90 days due to Redwood-caused scheduling or resource issues, Redwood will apply a pro rata credit of up to 50% of the implementation fee against the first month of service charges. This preserves non-refund baseline while providing a bounded remedy.

Option B: partial refund limited to fees for unperformed professional services (e.g., onsite engineering) where Redwood did not deliver a pre-agreed milestone and did not offer reasonable substitute timing within 30 days.

On the ramp language: propose we change the Order Form sentence from "reserved capacity to begin in month 2" to "reserved capacity to be provisioned and billable beginning on the first calendar day of month 1, subject to completion of onboarding milestones listed in Exhibit B". That ties the billing to milestones but preserves the implementation gating.

Ben — pricing impact if we commit to month-1 reserved capacity? Please confirm delta so Hannah can discuss commercial tradeoffs with Atlas.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@atlashealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA clause reconciliation + implementation fee — pricing delta

All —

If we move the reserved capacity to be billable from month 1 as Karthik proposed, the simplest commercial: bill 50% of the first-month reserved fee as an implementation ramp charge (applies toward month 1). That yields Atlas an earlier commitment without creating a full additional month invoice. If Atlas wants full month-1 reserved capacity invoiced as normal, delta is +1 month of reserved fee at the contracted rate.

I'll attach a short price table to the Drive link and can produce a one-page amendment showing the two options for their procurement team.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA clause reconciliation + implementation fee — acceptance of Option A (with edits)

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Atlas prefers Option A with one small edit: the credit should be capped at 40% (not 50%) and apply to the first two months of service (split equally) rather than only month 1. Atlas legal believes that provides a stronger operational buffer.

We also accept the ramp wording tied to Exhibit B milestones but need Exhibit B to list the specific onboarding checkpoints and target dates before we sign. Can you produce a draft Exhibit B and the one-page amendment showing the pricing delta (Ben's table) for procurement review?

I'll route the amendment internally as soon as I have those attachments.
